principle.name: Write Idiomatic Go
principle.description: Follow Go's idioms and conventions. Go code should be simple, clear, and readable. Avoid patterns from other languages that don't fit Go's design.
principle.rationale: Idiomatic Go code is easier to read, maintain, and understand by other Go developers. The Go community values simplicity over cleverness.

principle.name: Keep Functions Small
principle.description: Functions should do one thing and do it well. If a function is getting long or complex, break it into smaller functions.
principle.rationale: Small functions are easier to test, understand, and reuse. They also reduce cognitive load when reading code.

principle.name: Handle Errors Explicitly
principle.description: Always check errors and handle them appropriately. Never ignore errors without a clear reason and comment explaining why.
principle.rationale: Explicit error handling is a core feature of Go. Ignoring errors leads to silent failures and makes debugging difficult.

convention.rule: Define structs with clear field names

guidelines.guideline: Use pointer types for optional fields

practice.name: table_driven_tests
practice.description: Use table-driven tests for testing multiple scenarios with similar logic.

practice.name: test_helpers
practice.description: Create helper functions for common test setup.

practice.name: subtests
practice.description: Use t.Run() for organizing related tests.

practice.name: goroutine_lifecycle
practice.description: Always provide a way to stop goroutines.

practice.name: channel_closing
practice.description: Close channels only from the sender side.

practice.name: race_detection
practice.description: Run tests with race detector to find race conditions.

pitfall.why_problematic: Silent failures make debugging extremely difficult.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always handle errors. Use blank identifier only with a comment explaining why.

pitfall.why_problematic: Panic should only be used for unrecoverable errors. Normal errors should be returned.
pitfall.correct_approach: Return errors instead of panicking. Use panic only for truly exceptional conditions.

pitfall.why_problematic: Goroutines that never exit cause goroutine leaks and memory issues.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always provide a way to stop goroutines using context or done channels.

pitfall.why_problematic: Global mutable state makes code hard to test and can cause race conditions.
pitfall.correct_approach: Pass dependencies through function parameters or struct fields.
Check for nil before dereferencing pointers, especially from external sources.

category.name: after_writing
category.item: Run go vet for static analysis
Run go test -race for race detection
